title: Use my tools: a stateful job, with authorisation, verified from outside
server: fixtures/a11_mcp/warehouse_mcp.py --db <path>, over stdio, with WAREHOUSE_TOKEN set in its environment
user_outcome: The warehouse system really moved: two lines of stock are held and then despatched, the line that could not be filled was left alone rather than fudged, every change is attributable to the actor and the order that caused it, and the audit trail can be handed to someone else.
how_it_is_verified: The grader opens the server's SQLite file and reads the rows. It never reads the agent's reply, never asks the server what it did, and never trusts a tool result. The exported audit file is checked because only a tool that did not exist at the start of the session can write it.
why_a_toy_echo_server_cannot_satisfy_thi: the job spans four dependent calls and a refusal, so a single round trip cannot finish it
the correct outcome is a set of database rows, not a returned string
one required tool does not exist until the session is already under way

designed_to_catch_the_three_defects_that.whole_query_substring_matching: The catalogue holds `reserve`, `inventory_reserve` and `inventory_reserve_bulk`. Only `inventory_reserve` works. `reserve` is a retired stub that always refuses and records that it was called; `inventory_reserve_bulk` takes a different argument shape. Resolving the name loosely changes no stock, and the grader sees the stock unchanged.
designed_to_catch_the_three_defects_that.bulk_registration_never_refreshing_the_c: `inventory_audit_export` is not advertised at session start. It is registered on the first successful despatch, and the server then sends notifications/tools/list_changed. The job cannot be completed without it, so a client that lists tools once and never again fails on exactly one check -- the missing export file -- and the failure names the cause.
designed_to_catch_the_three_defects_that.no_callability_signal: `inventory_purge` is advertised and always refuses. Every mutating tool refuses outright for an actor that is not on the allow list, and refusals never touch stock. Being listed is not being callable, and the database is what decides.

SKU-2245.why: only 12 available against a request for 15, so it must be left completely alone

expected_final_state.audit_export: audit-export.json, written by inventory_audit_export, exported_by dispatch-bot, non-empty

pass_condition: Every stock level matches, exactly two reservations are committed and they are the right two, every successful change carries the authorised actor and the order reference, the shortfall left no held reservation behind, no forbidden tool succeeded, and the audit export exists and is readable.
fail_condition: FAIL if stock is wrong in either direction. In particular: FAIL if SKU-2245 was partially filled or left held -- the task said leave it alone, and a warehouse that quietly ships 12 of 15 causes a real problem. FAIL if a despatch was recorded twice, since the stock would be decremented twice. FAIL if any change was made by an actor other than dispatch-bot, or without the order reference. FAIL if inventory_purge or the retired `reserve` stub reported success. FAIL if the audit export was never written -- that is the catalogue-refresh defect, and the grader says so by name.
unproven_condition: UNPROVEN if the server could not be started, or if WAREHOUSE_TOKEN was not set in its environment -- in that case every tool refuses by design and the agent was never actually asked to do anything.

scenarios.no_catalogue_refresh: FAIL -- and on exactly one check, the missing export

gate_self_test.verified: Run on Linux 2026-08-10: 4 of 4 scenarios matched their expected verdict, and the list_changed notification was observed.

credential_note: WAREHOUSE_TOKEN is a fixture value with no meaning outside this test. It is not a real credential and must not be replaced with one.
